overview: Build the complete ASODEF S.A.S. digital platform as a single production-oriented delivery: a premium institutional website (React/Vite/TS), a modular NestJS/PostgreSQL backend, staff authentication with RBAC, a real Payment Center backed by a Bold PaymentProvider adapter built against Bold's official API docs, a full commercial CRM (prospects, leads, companies, business partners, affiliates, customers, beneficiaries, opportunities, proposals, agreements, contracts, plans/services), a full legal and policy center with versioned/approved documents, consent management, data-subject rights, data retention, cookie governance, PQR case management, commercial communications with suppression lists, refund/reversal/reconciliation workflows, an administrative platform, real reporting/dashboards, and audit logging throughout. Bold calls run in mock mode (no live network calls, no real credentials) until sandbox keys are supplied, and PRODUCTION_PAYMENTS_ENABLED stays false until every legal/commercial approval gate is APPROVED. Generated legal content is built as a real, versioned, admin-editable system populated with DRAFT content using only confirmed facts (company name, city, contact) — unconfirmed fields (legal representative, exact legal address, judicial notification email, prices, guarantees) stay explicitly unpublished/configurable rather than invented. The build ends with local Docker Compose verification, then — as a final gated milestone requiring explicit go-ahead — deployment to the existing ASODEF VPS under the new domain asodef.com.co, without touching the unrelated existing services already running on app.asodef.com.co, api.asodef.com.co, and webhook.asodef.com.co.
goals: Ship a premium, fully responsive, ASODEF-branded institutional website (Inicio, Quiénes somos, Beneficios, Portafolio, Cobertura, Empresas, Contacto) with real backend-served lead capture and content for key sections

Ship a working Payment Center (/pagos) covering lookup → order → provider handoff → result → receipt, backed by real domain modeling (obligations, orders, attempts, transactions, events, receipts) and a PaymentProvider adapter built to Bold's documented API shapes
Implement staff authentication (login, logout, password recovery, lockout) with seeded roles/permissions and an audit log foundation reusable by later phases
Verify the entire stack locally via Docker Compose (web, api, postgres, redis) with passing health checks before any deployment

Deploy Phase 1 to the ASODEF VPS under asodef.com.co (with www redirect) using paths /, /api, /pagos, /admin — while leaving the pre-existing app./api./webhook. subdomains and their services completely untouched
Establish patterns (status mapping, provider adapter interface, RBAC, audit) that the CRM, legal, and admin modules all reuse without rework

Ship a full commercial CRM covering the 14-stage pipeline (prospect through renewal/expiration) for prospects, leads, companies, business partners, affiliates, customers, and beneficiaries, with real dashboards backed by live data

Ship a full Legal & Policy Center (/legal/*) with versioned, approval-gated legal documents (privacy policy, data-processing policy, privacy notice, terms & conditions, payment terms, refund/reversal policy, cookie policy, PQR, accessibility, security) populated with DRAFT content from only confirmed facts
Ship consent management (purpose-scoped consent records with full evidence), a cookie preference center, and a data-subject-rights request workflow
Ship a PQR (peticiones/quejas/reclamos/sugerencias) case-management workflow with public submission and admin case handling
Ship contracts, plans/services versioning, business-partner lifecycle management, refunds/reversals, and reconciliation as real, persisted, audited workflows
Ship an administrative platform (/admin) exposing all of the above to authorized staff, backed entirely by real data — no fake dashboards

Enforce legal/commercial approval gates that keep PRODUCTION_PAYMENTS_ENABLED=false until every mandatory gate (NIT, legal address, corporate email, legal representative, policies, Bold production credentials, HTTPS, webhook validation, customer-service ownership) is APPROVED
nonGoals: No live Bold production payments — the adapter is built to the documented schema and runs in mock mode; PRODUCTION_PAYMENTS_ENABLED stays false until all legal/commercial approval gates are APPROVED and real sandbox/production credentials are supplied

No real outbound WhatsApp Business API or SMTP email dispatch — commercial/transactional notifications are fully modeled (templates, delivery records, suppression lists, retries) but the actual transport is a logging/persisting stub until real provider credentials are supplied

No invented legal representative, judicial notification email, final legal address, approved legal wording, refund guarantees, coverage guarantees, prices, partner companies, or plan conditions — these fields exist in the schema as configurable and stay unpublished/DRAFT until the user supplies validated values
No electronic-signature provider integration — ContractAcceptance supports recording acceptance evidence now; wiring a real e-signature vendor is out of scope until one is chosen

No customer/company self-service login portals (/mi-cuenta/*, /empresa/*) — all CRM, contracts, and legal-request handling in this build is operated by authorized staff through /admin; self-service portals are a distinct future build
No changes to the VPS's existing app.asodef.com.co, api.asodef.com.co, or webhook.asodef.com.co services, containers, ports, or Nginx server blocks
successMetrics: All Phase 1 routes render correctly at 320px, tablet, and 1440px+ without horizontal scroll
A full payment lookup → order → mock-Bold handoff → result → receipt flow completes end-to-end locally with correct status mapping and an audit trail entry per transition
docker compose up brings web, api, postgres, and redis to healthy status with zero manual intervention
lint, typecheck, unit/integration tests, production build, and the Playwright smoke test all pass in CI

After deployment, https://asodef.com.co and https://asodef.com.co/pagos respond over HTTPS, /api/v1/health returns 200, Postgres/Redis are not publicly reachable, and app.asodef.com.co / api.asodef.com.co / webhook.asodef.com.co remain reachable and unchanged
openQuestions: Bold webhook signature/authentication header format could not be found in the publicly fetched docs (webhook-specific page returned 404) — must be verified against the merchant's Bold dashboard or updated docs before enabling real webhook signature validation

Whether the /pagos/procesar mock-Bold handoff screen should visually mimic Bold's real checkout or use a clearly-labeled ASODEF 'modo prueba' placeholder — defaulting to the latter until real sandbox access exists
Exact copy/imagery for real ASODEF brand assets (logo, photography) — to be supplied later; Phase 1 wires placeholder assets at the final file paths

stack.framework: React 18 + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS (apps/web); NestJS + TypeScript (apps/api); Turborepo + pnpm workspaces monorepo
stack.hosting: Self-managed Contabo VPS (169.58.36.138, user asodefadmin) via Docker Compose + Nginx; new domain asodef.com.co (www redirects to apex); existing app./api./webhook. subdomains belong to another application and must not be modified
stack.database: PostgreSQL 16 via Prisma ORM; Redis for rate limiting, login-lockout counters, and webhook idempotency locks
stack.auth: Staff-only login in Phase 1. JWT access + refresh tokens carried in httpOnly, secure, SameSite cookies; server-side Session table for revocation; bcrypt password hashing; RBAC via seeded Roles/Permissions tables enforced by NestJS guards; login-attempt monitoring with Redis-backed lockout.

importFormat.description: Local/dev seed data shape used by the Prisma seed script to populate demo customers, obligations, and institutional content for Phase 1 testing. Not an end-user import feature.

rules: All monetary values are stored and computed as integer minor units (amountCents); never use floating-point arithmetic for money
A PaymentOrder transitions to APPROVED only after a verified provider confirmation (webhook event or authenticated status poll) — never from URL params, frontend state, or browser redirect alone
Public payment references are non-sequential, cryptographically random tokens — never expose the internal auto-increment/uuid ordering as a guessable sequence

Payment status enum is centrally defined once (DRAFT/PENDING/PROCESSING/APPROVED/REJECTED/FAILED/EXPIRED/CANCELLED/REFUNDED/PARTIALLY_REFUNDED) and mapped to Spanish labels in exactly one shared module consumed by both API responses and the frontend — no scattered string comparisons
Bold webhook events are processed idempotently keyed on a stable idempotency key derived from the provider transaction id + event type; duplicate deliveries must not double-process a transition

Webhook signature validation is implemented per Bold's documented pattern where available; because the specific webhook signature header could not be confirmed from public docs in this session, validation failures are logged and the event is still stored for later reconciliation — but no PaymentOrder transitions to APPROVED from an unverified signature once real signature validation ships (tracked as an open question)
PaymentReceipt records are created only for orders that have reached a verified APPROVED status — receipts are never generated for pending/rejected/failed orders
Payment lookup responses mask customer identification (e.g. show only last 4 digits) and never return full customer PII beyond what's needed to confirm identity
Every privileged or state-changing action (login, failed login, password reset, manual payment note, status transition) is written to AuditLog with actor, action, entity, and timestamp
Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (or argon2) and never logged; JWTs, session cookies, and Bold credentials are never written to logs

Bold API integration follows the fetched official docs verbatim: base URL https://api.online.payments.bold.co, POST /v1/payment-intent, GET /v1/payment-intent/{reference_id}, POST /v1/payment, GET /v1/payment/{reference_id}, header Authorization: x-api-key <llave_de_identidad>; any field not confirmed by docs is marked UNVERIFIED in code comments rather than invented

In Phase 1, BoldPaymentProvider makes no real outbound HTTP calls — it runs against an internal mock transport returning documented response shapes — until real sandbox credentials are supplied and explicitly enabled

The VPS deployment must never stop, restart, reconfigure, or overwrite the existing services on app.asodef.com.co, api.asodef.com.co, or webhook.asodef.com.co, their containers, or their Nginx server blocks
www.asodef.com.co must redirect (301) to https://asodef.com.co; the new platform is served under the apex domain using path-based routing (/, /api, /pagos, /admin), not new subdomains

A LegalDocumentVersion's approvedContent is only set (and only then can it move to PUBLISHED) after an authorized user with legal-approval permission explicitly approves it — draftContent may exist and be edited freely without ever implying public approval
The public /legal/* routes render only PUBLISHED LegalDocumentVersions; DRAFT/LEGAL_REVIEW/PENDING_APPROVAL content is never served publicly

No confirmed-missing legal fact (legal representative, exact registered address, judicial notification email, prices, guarantees, partner names, plan conditions) is ever invented as placeholder-that-looks-real; such fields are either omitted from public content or rendered as an explicit 'pendiente de confirmación' state in the admin view

Marketing/optional communications are sent only when a ConsentRecord for that purpose is GRANTED and the recipient is not present in SuppressionListEntry for that channel; transactional/service communications (payment result, PQR update) do not require marketing consent but always respect an explicit unsubscribe-from-marketing distinct from service messages

Cookie categories: 'strictly necessary' cookies always run; 'preferences', 'analytics', and 'marketing' cookies require an explicit, non-preselected ConsentRecord before any corresponding third-party script loads

PRODUCTION_PAYMENTS_ENABLED remains false and is enforced at the application layer (not just documented) until every ApprovalGate row is status=APPROVED and not expired; the BoldPaymentProvider refuses to switch out of mock mode while any gate is not APPROVED

A Refund or Reversal can only be created by a user holding payments.refund permission, requires a reason and links to the original PaymentOrder/PaymentTransaction, and is always audited; it never silently mutates the original transaction record

A BusinessPartner cannot move to a publication status visible on the public site until legal validation, commercial validation, benefit confirmation, agreement-validity confirmation, logo authorization, contact confirmation, and coverage confirmation are all recorded as complete
Every DataSubjectRequest and PqrCase carries a due date and status history; identity verification is required before any access/deletion/correction request is fulfilled

RetentionPolicy-driven anonymization/deletion requires an explicit approval before execution and always writes an AnonymizationLog evidence entry; legal-hold records are excluded from automatic retention actions regardless of elapsed retention period

stories.title: Scaffold monorepo, tooling, and local Docker Compose environment
stories.description: As a developer, I want a working Turborepo + pnpm workspaces monorepo with apps/web (Vite+React+TS), apps/api (NestJS+TS), and shared packages, plus a local Docker Compose stack, so that all later stories have a consistent foundation.
acceptanceCriteria: Run `pnpm install` at the repo root; `pnpm -w run dev` starts both apps/web (Vite dev server) and apps/api (NestJS in watch mode) concurrently via Turborepo
docker-compose.yml defines postgres:16 and redis:7 services with named volumes and healthchecks; `docker compose up -d postgres redis` reaches 'healthy' status for both
Repo contains apps/web, apps/api, packages/ui, packages/config, packages/typescript-config, packages/eslint-config with working package.json + tsconfig references between them

stories.title: Prisma schema and migration for auth/RBAC core entities + role/permission seed
stories.description: As a backend developer, I want the User/Role/Permission/Session/PasswordReset/LoginAttempt schema migrated and seeded so authentication and authorization stories have real tables to work against.
acceptanceCriteria: Prisma schema defines User, Role, Permission, UserRole, RolePermission, Session, PasswordReset, LoginAttempt matching the PRD dataModel, with UUID primary keys and createdAt/updatedAt timestamps
`pnpm --filter api prisma migrate dev` applies cleanly against the local postgres container

Seed script creates the 9 roles (SUPER_ADMIN, ADMIN, FINANCE, COMMERCIAL, CUSTOMER_SERVICE, COMPANY_PARTNER, AFFILIATE, CUSTOMER, AUDITOR) and the Phase 1-relevant permission keys (payments.read, payments.create, payments.reconcile, payments.refund, customers.read, audit.read, etc.)
Example: after seeding, querying Role where name='SUPER_ADMIN' returns exactly one row with all Phase 1 permissions attached
Negative case: re-running the seed script is idempotent — it does not create duplicate roles/permissions on a second run

stories.title: NestJS bootstrap: config validation, structured logging, health checks, Swagger
stories.description: As a backend developer, I want apps/api to validate its environment at startup, log in structured JSON, expose health endpoints, and publish an OpenAPI doc so the service is operable from day one.
acceptanceCriteria: ConfigModule validates required env vars (DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, JWT_SECRET, JWT_REFRESH_SECRET) at boot using zod or class-validator; missing/invalid values throw a startup error naming the offending variable (not its value)
GET /api/v1/health, /api/v1/health/live, /api/v1/health/ready are implemented; /ready checks Postgres and Redis connectivity
Swagger UI is served at /api/docs in non-production environments only
Structured logs (pino or nestjs built-in logger configured for JSON) include timestamp, level, context, and request id; no secrets are ever logged
Example: `curl :3000/api/v1/health/ready` returns 200 with `{status:'ok'}` when postgres/redis are up
Negative case: stopping the postgres container causes /api/v1/health/ready to return 503 within one health-check interval

stories.title: Frontend app shell: routing, TanStack Query, layouts, base UI components
stories.description: As a frontend developer, I want the full Phase 1 route tree, a TanStack Query client, and base layout/UI components so feature stories can slot in pages without re-plumbing routing.
acceptanceCriteria: React Router route tree covers all Phase 1 routes from the PRD's routes list, split into PublicLayout, AuthLayout, and PaymentLayout wrapper layouts
TanStack Query's QueryClientProvider wraps the app with sane defaults (retry, staleTime) and React Query Devtools enabled only in development
packages/ui exports at least Button, Card, Input, and FormField components styled per the design tokens from US-002, consumed by apps/web via workspace dependency
Example: navigating to /pagos/orden/abc123 renders inside PaymentLayout without the marketing Navbar/Footer
Negative case: navigating to an undefined route (e.g. /no-existe) renders a styled 404 page, not a blank screen or router crash

stories.title: Backend auth module: login, logout, JWT + refresh cookies, password hashing
stories.description: As a staff user, I want to log in and out securely so that protected areas of the platform can identify me.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/auth/login validates credentials with bcrypt, issues a short-lived JWT access token and a longer-lived refresh token, both set as httpOnly, secure, SameSite=strict cookies; POST /api/v1/auth/logout revokes the Session row and clears cookies
Session entity persists a hash of the refresh token (never the raw token) with expiresAt/revokedAt
Install: `pnpm --filter api add @nestjs/jwt bcrypt` (and `@types/bcrypt` as a dev dependency)
Example: logging in with a seeded test user returns 200 and sets both cookies; a subsequent authenticated request succeeds using the access token
Negative case: logging in with a wrong password returns 401 with a generic 'credenciales inválidas' message that does not reveal whether the email exists

stories.title: Password recovery flow with rate limiting
stories.description: As a staff user who forgot their password, I want to request and complete a reset so I can regain access without admin intervention.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset/request creates a PasswordReset row with a hashed, time-limited token and logs (stub, not real email) the reset link; always returns a generic success response regardless of whether the email exists
POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset/confirm validates the token, sets a new bcrypt-hashed password, marks the token usedAt, and revokes all existing Sessions for that user
Rate limiting (NestJS ThrottlerModule) caps reset requests per IP/email within a time window
Example: requesting a reset, then confirming with the correct token and a strong new password succeeds and old sessions are revoked
Negative case: confirming with an expired or already-used token returns a 400 error and does not change the password

stories.title: RBAC guards and audit log foundation
stories.description: As a backend developer, I want reusable Permissions/Roles guards and an AuditService so every protected/privileged endpoint in later stories enforces access control and leaves a trail.
acceptanceCriteria: A @RequirePermissions() decorator + PermissionsGuard reads the authenticated user's roles→permissions and allows/denies the request; applied via a simple example endpoint
AuditLog entity + AuditService.record(action, entityType, entityId, actorUserId, previous, next, req) is implemented and unit-testable independent of any specific module
Example: a request to a permission-guarded test endpoint from a user without the required permission returns 403
Negative case: a request with a valid but expired/tampered JWT is rejected by the guard chain before the permission check runs

stories.title: Login-attempt monitoring and account lockout
stories.description: As a security-conscious operator, I want repeated failed logins to trigger a temporary lockout so brute-force attempts are slowed down.
acceptanceCriteria: Every login attempt (success/failure) is recorded in LoginAttempt; a Redis-backed counter locks the account for a configurable window after N consecutive failures
Install: `pnpm --filter api add ioredis`
Example: 5 consecutive failed logins for the same email trigger a 429 'cuenta bloqueada temporalmente' response on the 6th attempt even with the correct password
Negative case: a successful login resets the failure counter for that email

stories.title: Frontend auth pages (login, forgot password, reset password)
stories.description: As a staff user, I want usable login/recovery screens so I can access protected areas from a browser.
acceptanceCriteria: /iniciar-sesion, /recuperar-clave, /restablecer-clave are implemented with React Hook Form + Zod validation, calling the US-006/US-007 endpoints via TanStack Query mutations

Example: submitting /iniciar-sesion with valid seeded credentials redirects to a protected placeholder route

stories.title: PaymentProvider interface and BoldPaymentProvider adapter (mock mode)

stories.title: Payment order creation service with status mapping and duplicate prevention

stories.title: Bold payment creation and status endpoints

stories.title: Bold webhook endpoint with idempotent async processing

stories.title: Legal document schema and versioning/approval workflow

stories.title: Consent purposes and consent record capture

Example: submitting the contact form creates one ConsentRecord for data_processing tied to the currently PUBLISHED tratamiento-de-datos version

stories.title: Cookie preference center

stories.title: Data-subject-rights request workflow

acceptanceCriteria: Prisma schema adds DataSubjectRequest with type enum (access, consultation, update, correction, deletion, revocation, proof-of-authorization, data-use-information, complaint, identity-verification, incident-report), status enum (RECEIVED/IDENTITY_VERIFICATION/IN_REVIEW/INFORMATION_REQUIRED/RESOLVED/REJECTED_WITH_REASON/CLOSED), dueDate, assignedUserId

/legal/solicitudes-de-datos public form posts to POST /api/v1/data-subject-requests (rate-limited, validated) creating a request in RECEIVED status and returning a tracking reference; an admin endpoint (data.manage permission) supports assignment, status transitions with required notes, and resolution

Example: submitting a deletion request returns a tracking reference; looking it up (public, reference-only, no auth) shows current status without exposing other requesters' data

stories.title: Data retention policies and anonymization/deletion evidence

A scheduled job (documented cron/worker, runnable on-demand for verification) identifies records past their retention window and NOT under legal hold, and requires an explicit admin approval (retention.manage permission) before anonymizing/deleting, writing an AnonymizationLog entry as evidence
Example: running the retention-review job against seeded data older than its configured window flags it for review without auto-deleting anything without approval
Negative case: a record flagged with legalHold=true is excluded from the retention-review candidate list even if past its retention window

stories.title: PQR case management

acceptanceCriteria: Prisma schema adds PqrCase with caseNumber (unique, non-sequential-looking), category, status enum (RECEIVED/ASSIGNED/IN_REVIEW/INFORMATION_REQUIRED/RESOLVED/CLOSED/REOPENED), priority, dueDate, optional links to customer/payment-order/contract

/legal/pqr public form posts to POST /api/v1/pqr-cases (validated, rate-limited) and returns the caseNumber; an admin endpoint (pqr.manage permission) supports assignment, status transitions with notes, resolution text, and capturing satisfactionScore after resolution
Every transition is audited; case creation triggers a CommunicationLog entry (US-059) acknowledging receipt
Example: submitting a PQR with category='reclamo' and a linked payment reference creates a case visible in the admin queue with that payment linked
Negative case: attempting to close a case still in INFORMATION_REQUIRED without a resolution note returns a validation error

stories.title: CRM core: Prospects, commercial contacts, opportunities, and the 14-stage pipeline

CommercialActivity supports scheduling and completing follow-up tasks tied to an opportunity, with an assigned user and due date
Example: promoting a lead to a Prospect, creating an Opportunity in new_prospect stage, and moving it to qualified produces one OpportunityStatusHistory row reflecting exactly that transition

stories.title: Proposals and agreements

Example: creating two Proposal versions for the same opportunity preserves both, with the latest flagged as current

stories.title: Business partner lifecycle and publication gate

A publish action (partners.manage permission) is only permitted when legal validation, commercial validation, benefit confirmation, agreement-validity confirmation, logo authorization, contact confirmation, and coverage confirmation are all recorded true; otherwise it returns 409 listing which checks are missing
Example: a partner with all six validations recorded true can be published and then appears via a public read-only partners endpoint
Negative case: a partner missing 'coverage confirmation' cannot be published — the API response names that specific missing validation

stories.title: Plan/service versioning and pre-payment disclosure
stories.description: As a customer, I want the exact plan/service terms I'm accepting to be shown and stored at the moment I pay, so there's no ambiguity about what I agreed to.
acceptanceCriteria: Plan schema expands to the full field set (internal/public name, description, coverage, includedServices, exclusions, eligibility, beneficiaryRules, priceCents, billingFrequency, taxes, startDate/endDate, version, status DRAFT/UNDER_REVIEW/ACTIVE/SUSPENDED/RETIRED/ARCHIVED, terms, cancellationRules, renewalRules, paymentConditions)

A pre-payment disclosure endpoint returns the exact ACTIVE plan/service version for a given obligation (name, description, total, currency, taxes, concept, frequency, terms, renewal/cancellation conditions, contact channel, PQR channel) and the PaymentOrder creation flow stores which exact plan version was disclosed/accepted
Example: creating a payment order for an obligation tied to Plan v2 records planVersionAcceptedId=2 on the order even if the plan is later edited to v3
Negative case: attempting to create a payment order for an obligation whose plan is not ACTIVE (e.g. SUSPENDED) returns 409

stories.title: Contracts: versioning, signers, acceptance, and private document storage
stories.description: As ASODEF's legal/commercial team, I want contracts tracked with versioned documents and recorded acceptance so partner/customer agreements are enforceable and auditable.
acceptanceCriteria: Prisma schema adds Contract (status 7-state enum DRAFT/UNDER_REVIEW/PENDING_ACCEPTANCE/ACTIVE/EXPIRED/CANCELLED/ARCHIVED), ContractVersion (private document path, checksum, uploadedBy), ContractSigner, ContractAcceptance (acceptance evidence: ipAddress, timestamp, evidenceReference)
Contract documents are stored outside any public web root; download requires an authenticated, permission-checked, time-limited signed URL (contracts.read permission) — never a public static path
Recording a ContractAcceptance requires the contract to be in PENDING_ACCEPTANCE and moves it to ACTIVE once all required signers have accepted
Example: uploading a new ContractVersion, adding two signers, and recording both acceptances transitions the contract from PENDING_ACCEPTANCE to ACTIVE
Negative case: requesting a contract document download without contracts.read permission returns 403; requesting an expired signed download URL returns 410

stories.title: Refund and reversal workflow
stories.description: As finance staff, I want refunds/reversals to require justification, evidence, and approval, and to be fully traceable back to the original payment.
acceptanceCriteria: Prisma schema adds Refund (amountCents, reason, evidencePath nullable, status, approvedByUserId nullable, providerReference nullable) linked to a PaymentOrder/PaymentTransaction

POST /api/v1/payments/:reference/refund (payments.refund permission) validates eligibility (order must be APPROVED, amount not exceeding original), requires a reason, creates a Refund in a pending-approval state, and only an approval action (separate permission) calls BoldPaymentProvider.createRefund (mock mode) and updates PaymentOrder status to REFUNDED or PARTIALLY_REFUNDED
Every refund/reversal step (request, evidence upload, approval, provider call, customer-facing communication trigger) is audited
Example: requesting and then approving a full refund for a mock-approved order transitions it to REFUNDED and logs a CommunicationLog entry notifying the customer
Negative case: a user with only payments.read (no payments.refund) attempting to request a refund gets 403; requesting a refund larger than the original amount returns 400

stories.title: Reconciliation module
stories.description: As finance staff, I want internal payment orders reconciled against provider transactions so mismatches (duplicate events, amount differences, unmatched approvals) are caught and tracked to resolution.
acceptanceCriteria: Prisma schema adds Reconciliation (runDate, responsibleUserId, differencesFound, resolutionStatus) and ReconciliationDifference (kind: provider-approved-internally-pending / internal-approved-no-provider-confirmation / duplicate-event / amount-mismatch / reference-mismatch / unprocessed-notification / refund-inconsistency)

A reconciliation run (payments.reconcile permission) compares PaymentOrder+PaymentTransaction+PaymentEvent+PaymentReceipt+Refund records for a date range and persists any differences found, each independently resolvable with notes

Example: manually creating a PaymentEvent that updates provider status to APPROVED without a corresponding internal transition, then running reconciliation, surfaces exactly one 'internal-approved-no-provider-confirmation' or matching difference record
Negative case: running reconciliation twice over the same already-resolved period does not duplicate previously-resolved ReconciliationDifference rows

stories.title: Legal/commercial approval gates and PRODUCTION_PAYMENTS_ENABLED enforcement
stories.description: As ASODEF's leadership, I want real payments hard-blocked until every legal/commercial prerequisite is formally approved, so the platform can't accidentally go live before it's ready.
acceptanceCriteria: Prisma schema adds ApprovalGate seeded with the 15 required gates (NIT, legal address, corporate email, legal representative, commercial registration, privacy policy, data-processing policy, terms and conditions, payment policy, refund/reversal procedure, PQR process, plan/service conditions, Bold production credentials, HTTPS, webhook validation, customer-service ownership), each starting PENDING

A config service exposes isProductionPaymentsEnabled() that returns true only when every ApprovalGate.status=APPROVED and none is expired; BoldPaymentProvider consults this before ever allowing BOLD_MODE to be anything other than mock
Admin endpoints (approvals.manage permission) transition gates through PENDING/UNDER_REVIEW/APPROVED/REJECTED/EXPIRED, each requiring approver, date, and optional supporting document/notes
Example: approving 14 of 15 gates still leaves isProductionPaymentsEnabled() returning false
Negative case: attempting to force BOLD_MODE=live via config while any gate is not APPROVED causes the API to fail startup/config validation rather than silently allowing live payments

stories.title: Commercial communications, templates, and suppression lists
stories.description: As ASODEF, I want all outbound communications (transactional and marketing) templated, logged, and consent/suppression-aware, so marketing never ignores an opt-out and every message is traceable.
acceptanceCriteria: Prisma schema adds CommunicationTemplate (key, channel, kind transactional/marketing, subject, body) and CommunicationLog (recipient, channel, status, attempts, errorCategory) and SuppressionListEntry (channel, recipient, reason)

A NotificationService.send(templateKey, recipient, data) stub persists a CommunicationLog row and logs the rendered content (no real SMTP/WhatsApp dispatch yet); for kind=marketing it checks ConsentRecord(optional_marketing)=GRANTED and SuppressionListEntry absence before persisting as 'would-send', otherwise records status=suppressed with a reason
An unsubscribe endpoint adds a SuppressionListEntry and revokes the optional_marketing ConsentRecord
Example: sending a marketing-kind template to a recipient with GRANTED consent and no suppression entry logs status='sent' (stub); the same call for a suppressed recipient logs status='suppressed'
Negative case: a transactional template (e.g. payment result) is still sent/logged even if the recipient revoked optional_marketing — the two are independent

stories.title: Evidencia de aceptacion electronica: vista de autoservicio 'Mis consentimientos'
stories.domain: A - Contenido legal y empresarial / B - Consentimientos
stories.description: Como usuario autenticado, quiero ver en /mi-cuenta un listado de mis propios consentimientos (proposito, version del documento aceptado, fecha, canal), para tener evidencia visible de lo que he aceptado, sin depender de pedirlo por soporte.
stories.businessValue: El lado admin de evidencia de consentimiento ya existe (ConsentController: GET /admin/consent-records de busqueda + detalle, gateado por data.manage), pero no existe ninguna vista de autoservicio para el propio titular. /mi-cuenta sigue siendo enteramente un RoutePlaceholder desde la refactorizacion premium - este story reemplaza esa placeholder con una primera pantalla real, sin construir todo mi-cuenta.
acceptanceCriteria: Nuevo endpoint GET /me/consent-records (o extension del existente) devuelve unicamente los ConsentRecord del actor autenticado (nunca de otro usuario) con: proposito, version del documento (si aplica), fecha/hora, canal, resultado (otorgado/revocado)
/mi-cuenta reemplaza el RoutePlaceholder por una seccion real 'Mis consentimientos' que consume ese endpoint - loading/error/empty states reales, no simulados
Ejemplo: un usuario con 3 registros de consentimiento (terms_and_conditions v2, cookie_preferences v1, commercial_communications otorgado) ve las 3 filas con su fecha real

Negativo: un usuario CUSTOMER no puede leer /me/consent-records de otro actor ni pasando su propio userId por query - el endpoint ignora cualquier id externo y usa exclusivamente el actor de la sesion
Negativo: un usuario sin ningun registro de consentimiento ve un EmptyState real, no un error
securityRequirements: El endpoint nunca acepta un userId/actorId como parametro externo - se deriva unicamente del JWT/sesion autenticada, para impedir IDOR (el mismo patron de bug que US-063 encontro y corrigio en refunds)
auditRequirements: La sola lectura de los propios registros no genera un nuevo AuditLog (es lectura de datos propios, no una accion administrativa)
testingRequirements: Backend: test de integracion confirma que el endpoint filtra por el actor autenticado y rechaza intentos de leer registros ajenos
Frontend: test de la nueva seccion de /mi-cuenta con datos reales mockeados + el caso vacio
outOfScope: Reconstruir el resto de /mi-cuenta (sigue siendo placeholder fuera de esta seccion)
Permitir revocar consentimientos desde esta pantalla (eso es US-073)
stories.notes: IDOR-safety pattern follows the real US-063 refunds fix already in this codebase.

stories.title: Auditoria y vinculacion real de consentimientos en los formularios restantes
stories.description: Como responsable de cumplimiento, quiero que cada formulario relevante (contacto, registro, pagos, PQR, DSR, CRM, empresa, contratos) muestre el texto legal exacto y registre el ConsentRecord correcto con proposito+version+fecha+hora+IP+user agent+canal+actor+formulario+evidencia, para que ningun formulario capture datos sin el consentimiento correspondiente correctamente enlazado.
stories.businessValue: US-046/047/048 ya construyeron el mecanismo de ConsentService.record() y el catalogo de 8 propositos; este story es una auditoria literal (no una reconstruccion) para confirmar cuales de los formularios listados por la directiva ya estan correctamente enlazados y corregir los que no.
acceptanceCriteria: Se audita, formulario por formulario, cual consent purpose aplica y si el formulario ya lo registra: contacto (data_processing), registro/auth (terms_and_conditions + data_processing), pagos (payment_terms), PQR (data_processing), DSR (data_processing), CRM (n/a si es interno, o data_processing si el prospecto se auto-registra), empresa/alianzas (data_processing + contract_acceptance si aplica), contratos (contract_acceptance)

Cualquier formulario de la lista que hoy NO enlaza su consent purpose correspondiente se corrige para hacerlo, mostrando el texto legal exacto de la version PUBLISHED vigente (nunca un resumen ni una version distinta a la aceptada)
Ejemplo real: si el formulario de contacto ya registra data_processing correctamente (a verificar en el codigo), se documenta como ya conforme, sin duplicar trabajo

Negativo: un formulario que requiere consentimiento y el usuario no lo marca no debe permitir el envio (ya sea deshabilitando el submit o rechazando en backend con 400) - se verifica el comportamiento real en al menos un formulario corregido

Todo test que necesite un documento PUBLISHED para verificar el flujo usa el patron ya establecido de publish-then-restore (publish-legal-document-for-test.ts / e2e/support/legal-documents.ts) - nunca se publica un documento y se deja publicado como efecto colateral de una prueba
securityRequirements: Ningun formulario nuevo relaja los consentimientos obligatorios ya exigidos por historias previas
auditRequirements: Cada ConsentRecord nuevo sigue registrando actor, canal, formulario de origen e IP/user-agent tal como ya lo hace ConsentService.record()
testingRequirements: Un test de integracion por cada formulario corregido (no por cada formulario ya conforme, que solo se documenta)
Al menos un e2e real que confirma el bloqueo de envio sin consentimiento en un formulario corregido
outOfScope: Modificar el catalogo de 8 ConsentPurpose (se reutiliza el existente)
Formularios puramente internos de staff que no involucran datos del titular (p. ej. formularios admin de gestion CRM que no son autoservicio)
stories.notes: This is an audit-first story: implementation only touches forms found to be genuinely non-conformant, per user's explicit 'no dupliques historias ya implementadas' instruction.

stories.title: Revocacion de consentimientos comerciales (autoservicio)
stories.description: Como usuario, quiero poder revocar mi consentimiento de comunicaciones comerciales/WhatsApp/marketing opcional desde 'Mis consentimientos', para dejar de recibir comunicaciones comerciales sin afectar los mensajes transaccionales que sigo necesitando.
stories.businessValue: Ninguna ruta 'revoke' existe hoy en el modulo de consent (confirmado por busqueda en el codigo) - es una funcionalidad real y ausente, explicitamente exigida por la directiva ('permitir revocacion', 'bloquear envios comerciales cuando el consentimiento sea revocado').
acceptanceCriteria: Nuevo endpoint POST /me/consent-records/:purpose/revoke (solo para propositos revocables: commercial_communications, optional_marketing - nunca para terms_and_conditions/data_processing/payment_terms, que son condiciones de servicio, no consentimientos revocables unilateralmente)
La revocacion crea un nuevo ConsentRecord con resultado 'revoked' (o el enum equivalente) preservando el historial completo - nunca se borra el registro de aceptacion original

Cualquier envio de comunicaciones comerciales (el mecanismo de NotificationService.send() de US-059) verifica el estado vigente de commercial_communications/optional_marketing antes de enviar un mensaje de tipo comercial, y lo bloquea si esta revocado - los mensajes transaccionales (confirmacion de pago, recibo, etc.) nunca se filtran por este consentimiento
Ejemplo: un usuario revoca commercial_communications; un intento posterior de envio de una plantilla de tipo marketing para ese usuario no se despacha (se registra como omitido, no como error)
Negativo: intentar revocar terms_and_conditions devuelve 400 (proposito no revocable)
La UI de 'Mis consentimientos' (US-071) agrega un boton de revocar solo sobre los propositos revocables, con confirmacion antes de ejecutar
securityRequirements: El endpoint de revocacion opera exclusivamente sobre el actor autenticado (mismo patron anti-IDOR que US-071)
auditRequirements: La revocacion es un evento auditable de habeas data - se registra igual que cualquier ConsentRecord, con actor/fecha/canal
testingRequirements: Backend: test que revoca y luego confirma que NotificationService.send() omite el envio comercial correspondiente
Backend: test negativo de revocar un proposito no revocable
Frontend: test del boton de revocar con confirmacion
outOfScope: Permitir revertir una revocacion con un simple 'deshacer' (el usuario debe volver a otorgar el consentimiento explicitamente, con el mismo flujo de aceptacion)
stories.notes: Confirmed via grep: no 'revoke'/'revocar' string exists anywhere in apps/api/src/modules/consent or apps/web before this story.

stories.title: Endpoint real de creacion de empresa (admin)
stories.description: Como administrador, quiero crear una empresa desde un endpoint real (no desde Prisma manual), con validacion de NIT unico, normalizacion de datos y auditoria, para que dar de alta una empresa deje de depender de un workaround manual.
stories.businessValue: CompaniesController hoy solo expone GET (list, findById) - no existe POST. El permiso companies.manage ya existe en el catalogo RBAC (rbac-catalog.spec.ts lo referencia explicitamente) pero ningun endpoint lo usa todavia: la base de permisos esta lista, falta la operacion.
acceptanceCriteria: Nuevo POST /admin/companies gateado por @RequirePermissions('companies.manage') (no companies.read)

CreateCompanyDto valida: NIT (formato colombiano, unico - @@unique constraint + verificacion aplicativa con mensaje claro), razon social (requerida), nombre comercial (opcional), contacto (nombre+telefono/email), direccion, ciudad, departamento, estado inicial
El NIT se normaliza (sin puntos/guiones extra, formato consistente) antes de la comprobacion de unicidad y antes de guardar
La respuesta nunca incluye campos internos sensibles innecesarios - sigue el mismo patron de 'respuesta publica segura' que US-053 establecio para business partners
Se registra un AuditLog (mismo mecanismo ya usado en pagos/legal/consent) con el actor creador, la empresa creada y timestamp
Ejemplo: crear una empresa con NIT nuevo y datos completos devuelve 201 con la empresa creada
Negativo: crear una empresa con un NIT que ya existe devuelve 409 (Conflict) con mensaje claro, sin crear una fila duplicada
Negativo: un actor sin companies.manage (p. ej. solo companies.read) recibe 403
securityRequirements: companies.manage requerido explicitamente - companies.read (ya usado por list/findById) nunca es suficiente para creacion
Prevencion de duplicados por NIT normalizado, no solo por igualdad de string cruda
auditRequirements: AuditLog obligatorio en la creacion, siguiendo el patron ya generalizado en 5 dominios previos (pagos, legal, consent, DSR, PQR, CRM)
testingRequirements: Test de integracion: creacion exitosa, 409 por NIT duplicado, 403 por permiso insuficiente, normalizacion del NIT
outOfScope: Edicion o eliminacion de empresas (solo creacion, que es el gap literal reportado)
stories.notes: Verified live: CompaniesController (apps/api/src/modules/companies/companies.controller.ts) has only 2 GET routes; companies.manage already exists in rbac-catalog.spec.ts unused.

stories.title: UI admin de creacion de empresa
stories.description: Como administrador, quiero un formulario en el panel admin para crear una empresa usando el nuevo endpoint, con validacion y estados de error reales, para no depender de herramientas fuera de la aplicacion.
stories.businessValue: Completa el flujo end-to-end de US-074 - sin esta UI el endpoint solo seria accesible por API directa, lo cual no resuelve el problema operativo real que motiva este dominio.
acceptanceCriteria: Nueva pantalla o dialogo 'Nueva empresa' accesible desde la lista de empresas admin existente, gateada por companies.manage (el boton no aparece para actores sin el permiso)
Formulario con los mismos campos del DTO de US-074, validacion en cliente (NIT, campos requeridos) antes de enviar

Estados reales: cargando, error de validacion (mensajes especificos por campo cuando el backend los devuelve), 409 por NIT duplicado mostrado de forma clara, exito (la empresa nueva aparece en la lista sin recargar la pagina completa)
Ejemplo: completar el formulario con datos validos crea la empresa y la lista se actualiza
Negativo: enviar el formulario con un NIT ya existente muestra el error 409 sin perder los datos ya escritos
securityRequirements: El boton/formulario completo esta ausente (no solo deshabilitado) para actores sin companies.manage, siguiendo el patron ya usado en el resto del admin
auditRequirements: Ninguna auditoria adicional en el frontend - la auditoria ocurre en el backend (US-074)
testingRequirements: Test de componente: envio exitoso, error de validacion, 409 por duplicado
e2e: flujo completo de crear una empresa desde el admin y verla aparecer en la lista
outOfScope: Edicion de empresas existentes desde esta misma pantalla

stories.title: Cola de export jobs durable basada en Postgres
stories.description: Como plataforma, necesito que los ExportJob sobrevivan un reinicio del proceso y nunca se procesen dos veces por dos instancias concurrentes, para eliminar la deuda tecnica documentada explicitamente en el propio codigo de ReportsService.processExportJob (comentario: 'si el proceso reinicia a mitad de export, el job simplemente queda PROCESSING para siempre - aceptable para este despliegue de revision; un rollout de produccion real necesitaria una cola durable').
stories.businessValue: Evaluacion arquitectonica explicita (segun lo pedido): NO se agrega BullMQ/Redis como dependencia nueva. El modelo ExportJob ya vive en Postgres y el volumen de exportaciones de esta plataforma no justifica una infraestructura de colas adicional; una cola durable basada en las mismas garantias transaccionales de Postgres (UPDATE ... WHERE status='PENDING' RETURNING, con lease/heartbeat) resuelve el problema real sin nueva infraestructura.
acceptanceCriteria: Migracion agrega a ExportJob: leaseOwner (String?, id del worker que reclamo el job), leaseExpiresAt (DateTime?), attemptCount (Int, default 0), maxAttempts (Int, default 3), nextAttemptAt (DateTime?), failedAt (DateTime?) - completedAt/errorMessage ya existen y se reutilizan

El reclamo de un job es atomico: una transaccion Prisma que hace UPDATE ... SET status='PROCESSING', leaseOwner=$workerId, leaseExpiresAt=now()+lease WHERE id=$id AND status IN ('PENDING') (o su expresion equivalente en Prisma) - dos workers que intentan reclamar el mismo job nunca ambos tienen exito

Un proceso 'recuperador' al arrancar (o en un intervalo) busca jobs PROCESSING cuyo leaseExpiresAt ya paso (lease vencido = proceso caido) y los vuelve a PENDING con attemptCount+1, o los marca FAILED si attemptCount >= maxAttempts
Reintentos usan nextAttemptAt para espaciar los intentos (backoff simple, ej. exponencial acotado) - no reintenta inmediatamente en bucle
Ejemplo: se simula un job PROCESSING con leaseExpiresAt en el pasado (proceso caido) - el recuperador lo vuelve a PENDING y un segundo processExportJob lo completa exitosamente
Ejemplo: dos llamadas concurrentes de reclamo sobre el mismo job - solo una tiene efecto, la otra no encuentra filas que actualizar
Negativo: un job que agota maxAttempts termina en FAILED con errorMessage descriptivo, nunca reintenta indefinidamente
El endpoint de descarga (getJobFilePath) sigue exigiendo status=READY - ningun cambio de comportamiento para el consumidor final

La decision arquitectonica (Postgres-durable vs BullMQ) queda documentada explicitamente en un comentario en el propio ExportJob del schema.prisma, igual que el comentario que ya documenta la limitacion actual
securityRequirements: El leaseOwner (worker id) no expone informacion sensible - es un identificador interno, nunca visible en las respuestas al usuario final
auditRequirements: Cada transicion de estado (reclamo, expiracion de lease, reintento, fallo definitivo) queda en el propio ExportJob (attemptCount/failedAt) como registro suficiente - no se requiere un AuditLog adicional para un mecanismo interno de procesamiento
testingRequirements: Test de integracion de reclamo atomico bajo dos llamadas concurrentes
Test de recuperacion de un job con lease vencido
Test de agotamiento de reintentos -> FAILED
Test de que el endpoint de descarga sigue funcionando igual (regresion)
outOfScope: Agregar BullMQ, Redis, o cualquier cola externa (evaluado y descartado explicitamente)
Coordinacion multi-instancia mas alla de lo que el lease atomico de Postgres ya resuelve (no se agrega un sistema de eleccion de lider separado)
stories.notes: Verified live: reports.service.ts's own comment already documents this exact gap before this story existed.

stories.title: Logo oficial: favicon, metadata social y comprobantes
stories.description: Como visitante o titular, quiero ver el logo oficial de ASODEF en la pestana del navegador, al compartir un enlace en redes sociales, y en mis comprobantes de pago, para que la identidad de marca sea consistente en todas las superficies restantes que aun no la usan.
stories.businessValue: Verificacion real confirma 3 huecos concretos: (1) apps/web/index.html no tiene ningun <link rel="icon"> ni existe archivo de favicon en apps/web/public/; (2) og:image/twitter:image apuntan a og-image.webp (un placeholder generico, no el isotipo real) y el JSON-LD de Organization omite explicitamente el campo logo con un comentario que dice que no habia asset disponible - el asset SI existe ahora (apps/web/src/assets/asodef-logo*.webp, integrados en la correccion de frontend publico); (3) ReceiptViewPage.tsx no importa ni renderiza BrandLogo en absoluto.
acceptanceCriteria: Se genera un favicon real (ico/png/svg segun corresponda) a partir del isotipo oficial (asodef-logo-icon.webp) y se enlaza en index.html con los tags <link rel="icon"> estandar (incluye variante para dispositivos Apple si aplica)
og:image y twitter:image se actualizan para usar un asset derivado del logo/isotipo oficial real, no el og-image.webp generico actual
El JSON-LD de Organization en index.html agrega el campo logo apuntando al asset real, eliminando el comentario que explicaba su ausencia
ReceiptViewPage.tsx importa y renderiza BrandLogo (el mismo componente compartido ya usado en navbar/footer/auth) en el encabezado del comprobante

Verificacion visual real (Chromium) confirma: la pestana del navegador muestra el favicon, y un comprobante renderizado muestra el logo con fondo transparente (continuando la validacion de transparencia ya hecha en esta sesion)

Negativo: ningun asset de logo nuevo se genera re-dibujando el logo (color/proporcion/tipografia/simbolo intactos) - solo se recortan/exportan formatos a partir de los archivos oficiales ya integrados
testingRequirements: Test de que ReceiptViewPage renderiza el componente BrandLogo
Verificacion manual en Chromium del favicon y de un og:image render (p. ej. via debugger de metadatos) confirmando el asset correcto
outOfScope: Rediseñar el logo o crear variantes de marca nuevas
Metadata social para paginas distintas de la home (og:image por ruta especifica), salvo que ya existiera ese patron
stories.notes: Verified live via grep: no favicon link/file exists; ReceiptViewPage.tsx has zero references to Logo/logo before this story.

stories.title: Revision visual real post-rebuild y correcciones
stories.domain: F - Revision visual real y rebuild
stories.description: Como responsable de calidad visual, quiero verificar en un navegador real (Chromium), en 1440/768/390px, cada una de las rutas afectadas por esta ampliacion del PRD, para confirmar que lo implementado luce realmente premium/institucional y no solo pasa las pruebas automatizadas.
stories.businessValue: Cierra la ampliacion completa con la misma disciplina de verificacion visual en vivo ya aplicada durante la Fase 2 de rediseño premium (11 commits previos), extendida a las superficies nuevas de esta ampliacion (mis-consentimientos, historial de versiones admin, creacion de empresa admin, favicon/comprobantes).
acceptanceCriteria: Rebuild final (dependencias, build del monorepo, imagenes Docker) posterior a que todas las historias US-068 a US-077 esten cerradas

Se capturan y verifican en Chromium, en 1440px/768px/390px, como minimo: home, /legal (lista con los 10 tipos nuevos), un documento legal nuevo, /mi-cuenta (seccion Mis consentimientos), /login, /pagos, /empresa, /admin (dashboard), /admin/usuarios, /admin (CRM), /admin (PQR), /admin (DSR), /admin/legal (historial de versiones), /admin/pagos, /admin/reportes, /admin/companies (nuevo formulario de creacion), /admin (comunicaciones)

Se compara el contenido servido contra el codigo fuente actual (grep de tokens recientes en el bundle servido, tal como se verifico el hash-mismatch de Vite en el rebuild inicial) para descartar cache/bundle obsoleto
Cualquier pantalla que sea funcional pero visualmente basica ('cumple pero no impresiona') se corrige antes de cerrar este story - no se da por terminada solo porque pasa los tests
Verificacion de accesibilidad basica: foco visible, contraste, ausencia de scroll horizontal en los 3 breakpoints, en cada una de las rutas listadas
Se documentan los hallazgos y correcciones en un commit separado si son necesarios ajustes adicionales de UI
testingRequirements: Suite completa: backend, frontend, e2e, lint, typecheck, build - todos en verde antes de considerar la ampliacion cerrada
outOfScope: Cambios de paleta de marca o tipografia fuera de refinamientos ya establecidos en la Fase 2 previa
stories.notes: Final story of the extension - gates closing the whole US-068..US-077 arc, mirroring the Fase 2 premium redesign's own final QA section.
